title: Weight separation
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and fix an isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ and an indeterminate $T$. Let
$X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper
cohomological family.
Interpret ordinary and reciprocal roots by the
root convention, and use the
absolute-value weight condition. Assume
that, for every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, every reciprocal root
$\alpha$ of $P_{i,\ell}$ satisfies

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}.
$$

Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series. Assume the
trace-to-determinant identity

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\Ql(T).
$$

For all integers $0\leq i,j\leq2d$ with
$i\neq j$, the polynomials $P_{i,\ell}$ and $P_{j,\ell}$ have no common
ordinary root in $\Qlb$ and are coprime in $\Qlb[T]$. Define the
odd and even parity products by

$$
N_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ odd}}}
P_{i,\ell}(T),
\qquad
D_\ell(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq2d\\ i\text{ even}}}
P_{i,\ell}(T).
$$

They are coprime, have constant coefficient $1$, and the
Hasse–Weil zeta series satisfies

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\frac{N_\ell(T)}{D_\ell(T)}
$$

after coefficient extension to $\Ql[[T]]$. More precisely, the ordinary
root multiset of each $P_{i,\ell}$ is exactly the submultiset of roots of
the appropriate parity product whose reciprocal $\alpha$ satisfies

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
$$

for the fixed isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$.

proof.text:
Fix $i\ne j$ and suppose that $\beta\in\Qlb$ is a common ordinary root of
$P_{i,\ell}$ and $P_{j,\ell}$. By [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots],
$\beta\ne0$ and $\alpha=\beta^{-1}$ is a reciprocal root of both factors.
The assumed weight condition therefore gives
$|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}=q^{j/2}$. Since $q=p^a>1$ for the prime $p$ and
$a\ge1$ in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], the function
$n\mapsto q^{n/2}$ is strictly increasing on the integers, so this equality
forces $i=j$, a contradiction. Thus distinct factors have no common ordinary
root. Regard the coefficient extensions of $P_{i,\ell}$ and $P_{j,\ell}$ as
polynomials over the algebraically closed field $\Qlb$; applying
[lem-zeta-coprime-no-common-root] to the absence of a common evaluation zero
shows that they are coprime in $\Qlb[T]$.

proof.text:
Let $O$ and $E$ be the finite odd and even index sets in the definition
[def-weil-parity-products], so that $N_\ell=\prod_{i\in O}P_{i,\ell}$ and
$D_\ell=\prod_{j\in E}P_{j,\ell}$. For a fixed odd $i$, Step 1 gives
$\operatorname{IsCoprime}(P_{i,\ell},P_{j,\ell})$ for every even $j$; applying
[lem-zeta-coprime-product] (and symmetry of coprimality) gives
$\operatorname{IsCoprime}(P_{i,\ell},D_\ell)$. Applying the same finite-product
lemma over all odd $i$ gives
$\operatorname{IsCoprime}(N_\ell,D_\ell)$. The smooth-proper family has
$P_{i,\ell}(0)=1$ for every $i$ by
[def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family], and the constant coefficient of
a finite product is the product of the constant coefficients; hence
$N_\ell(0)=D_\ell(0)=1$.

proof.text:
The assumed trace-to-determinant identity is
$Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ in $\Ql(T)$, where
$Z(X_0,T)$ is the point-count series of [def-weil-point-counts-zeta]. By the
parity definitions, $(-1)^{i+1}=1$ for odd $i$ and $-1$ for even $i$, so the
finite product is $N_\ell(T)D_\ell(T)^{-1}$. Step 2 gives $D_\ell(0)=1$;
therefore $D_\ell$, regarded in $\Ql[[T]]$, is a unit by
[lem-weil-power-series-unit-constant-coefficient]. The rational-function
identity consequently has the Taylor expansion
$Z(X_0,T)=N_\ell(T)/D_\ell(T)$ in $\Ql[[T]]$, which is the asserted
coefficient-extension statement.

proof.text:
For each $j$, [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization] factors the coefficient
extension of $P_{j,\ell}$ over $\Qlb$ as a finite product
$\prod_{\alpha\in R_j}(1-\alpha T)$, where $R_j$ is its reciprocal-root
multiset with algebraic multiplicities. Multiplying these factorizations over
all odd (respectively even) indices gives a factorization of $N_\ell$
(respectively $D_\ell$) by the multiset union of the $R_j$. The uniqueness
clause of the same node identifies this union with the reciprocal-root
multiset of the parity product, including multiplicities. By Step 1 no
ordinary root occurs in two distinct factors, and the assumed weight condition
puts every element of $R_j$ at absolute value $q^{j/2}$. Since $q>1$, the
values $q^{j/2}$ are distinct; filtering the reciprocal roots of $N_\ell$ by
$|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ therefore selects exactly $R_i$ when $i$ is odd,
and the analogous filtering of $D_\ell$ selects exactly $R_i$ when $i$ is
even. Inverting the reciprocal-root bijection from
[def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots] gives the asserted ordinary-root
multiset identifications.
